numeric_complexity_contract.reference: for every left end, extend the right end while keeping a running sum of the strict middle and compare it with both ends
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: with prefix sums P, segment l..r is stable when capacity[l] == capacity[r] and P[r] - P[l + 1] == capacity[r]; scan r from left to right, make left end l = r - 2 available by counting the key (capacity[l], P[l + 1]) in a hash map, and add the count of key (capacity[r], P[r] - capacity[r])

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: keep every valid reading in arrival order and rescan all of them for each query
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: sparse Fenwick trees (hash maps keyed by tree index over timestamps 0..1e6) holding the lux sum and the reading count, plus the latest (timestamp, lux) pair updated with >= so later arrivals win ties; a range query subtracts two prefix queries
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(log T) per call, T = 1e6 + 1 timestamp slots/O(r log T) space, r = valid readings

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: compare every token with every abusive word of the same length, position by position
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: build a trie of the abusive words; for each token keep the set of trie nodes reachable so far, advancing through the child equal to a letter or the children named by a symbol's substitutions, and report the token when a reached node ends a word
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(total token length * reachable trie nodes) worst case, O(total word length) to build/O(total word length) space
